note: THE DIVERGENCE. Emacs' beginning-of-buffer and end-of-buffer are commands that push the mark, so C-x C-x returns you to where you were; kg's are goto-char sugar and leave the mark alone. kg's `set-mark' additionally lights the region up, which a Lisp call has no business doing, and kg has no unhighlighted push-mark to use instead. The Emacs manual's own advice for Lisp code is (goto-char (point-min)), which is what these are.
